- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (sentiment > 0.5) — especially after recent spikes — and adjust downward by 5–15% for 3–5 day horizons.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (sentiment < 0.3) — particularly when sentiment drops sharply — and add 3–8% to forecast for 10+ day horizons.
- Avoid over-optimistic 30-day forecasts after recent price declines; apply mean reversion bias: if 10-day low is below 65, forecast should not exceed 68 unless sentiment > 0.7.
- Lagged sentiment (e.g., 3–5 day sentiment) often predicts 7–10 day price direction — use as a filter for 15+ day forecasts.
- Overshoot after spikes: if forecast exceeds 75 after a 70+ spike, reduce by 10–15% for next 5 days unless sentiment remains high.
- If sentiment is flat (0.2–0.4) over 3+ days, reduce forecast volatility — avoid sharp moves unless confirmed by 2+ consecutive sentiment > 0.5.
